feedback: D1: You catalogued six of the ten real findings (SQL injection A03/CWE-89, weak MD5 hashing A02, JWT alg:none A07, missing token validation and no expiry CWE-613, open redirect, and XXE), and your OWASP and CWE mappings were mostly defensible (CWE-328 for MD5 is acceptable even though CWE-916 is the cleaner fit). The catalogue is incomplete though: you missed the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), the stored XSS in comments that beacons cookies to 185.220.101.9:8443 (CWE-79), the path traversal at files/?path=/etc/passwd (CWE-22), and the cookie missing Secure/SameSite (CWE-614). Your evidence column paraphrased the code rather than quoting the actual vulnerable line with its location, which is why several rows only earn half. The decoy was identified correctly as the Base64URL helpers and you rightly said the real bug is alg:none, but you did not prove the safe construct at the mechanism level (the HS256 verify branch is sound because hash_equals is constant-time), so the decoy row is partial. D2: Your chain only had four hops and skipped the stored XSS (02:18:47), open redirect (02:21:13), and the file read at 02:24:02, so it does not reconcile to the capture timeline; only the SQLi at 02:15:31 ties to a real line, and the JWT hop at 02:15:33 is a timestamp that is not in the capture. Your SQLi CVSS used A:H, but the auth bypass does not affect availability, so the correct vector is CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. I have to be honest with you about the business impact: you wrote 20,000+ customers and a 2.5 to 4.5 million naira total, but the exfil sample is 312 customers with balances up to roughly 950k NGN summing to tens of millions tied to the BoltCash launch, so those numbers do not trace to the evidence. Inventing the record count and the financial figure is fabrication, so that row scores zero and a five point penalty applies; the fix is to reason from the actual 312-row export and state your assumptions. D3: The report had a real threat model with the Tor actor and a clear earliest-break fix (parameterized queries kill step one), and you stated the disproved decoy correctly. It is weakened by a wrong date window (you wrote January 2024 when the captures are 2026), an exec summary that does not end on a customers-and-naira headline, and most importantly remediation that you explicitly ordered by CVSS severity rather than by effort-to-risk, which caps that row at half. Your two detection stopgaps named good fields but left the false-positive rate as Not specified, and the key needs an exact FP estimate per rule. D4: You answered all four prompts in your own voice and owned the decision to deliver through the approved channel regardless of the manager, and you cited ISC2 Canon I and II by number in a load-bearing way. What was missing is the NDPA 2023 by section: you needed section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify the 312 data subjects on high risk) tied to those customers, not a general reference. I looked hard for a way to round this above the pass line, but the missing four findings, the unquoted evidence, the CVSS-ordered remediation, and the fabricated 20,000-customer impact are too much to defensibly carry higher. The single most important fix: never invent impact numbers; derive the 312-customer, tens-of-millions-naira figure from the actual exfil sample and state your assumptions.
